issues.description: Loop invariant on fixed_audio_packet_size buffer ignores non-audio payloads, allowing reordering
issues.detail: The send buffer's invariant is implicit: 'when packet_bytes is set, all bytes payloads are audio.' But serialize() returns bytes for audio and may return JSON strings for control. If a future bytes-typed control payload appears, it would be packetized as PCM. State the invariant: this branch handles audio only; document or guard by type/intent rather than payload type.

issues.description: Termination of buffered audio is not guaranteed; tail bytes may never be flushed
issues.detail: The while-loop only emits full packet_bytes chunks; any remainder less than packet_bytes lingers indefinitely. On stream end or speaker silence the final partial packet is silently dropped. State and enforce a flush invariant: on EndFrame or stop, pad-and-send or explicitly discard with a logged decision. Otherwise termination of the audio stream is informal.

issues.description: No real-time pacing despite docstring claim of 'real-time pacing'
issues.detail: The changelog and code comments promise 'strict framing and real-time pacing,' but the implementation only fixes packet size; it sends as fast as _write_frame is called. If Vonage requires 20ms cadence, this will burst. Either implement pacing using _send_interval/_next_send_time for the packetized path, or correct the documentation to claim only fixed framing.

issues.description: Wrong data structure for byte buffering: bytearray slice-delete is O(n) per packet
issues.detail: Repeated del self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes] copies the tail on every iteration, giving O(n) per emission and O(n*k) per call for k packets. For a streaming audio path this is asymptotically wasteful. A collections.deque of chunks with a small read-cursor, or memoryview windowing, would be O(1) amortized. Not hot today, but the right structure costs nothing.

issues.description: DTMF parsing accepts ambiguous schemas without documenting the contract
issues.detail: deserialize tries message.get('digit') then message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') with a comment 'Vonage may send digit in different formats.' Either the protocol spec pins one shape (cite it and remove the other branch) or both are real (document which firmware/version emits which). 'May' is not a specification a careful reader can verify.

issues.description: Resampler return contract is unaudited; len() check assumes a sized type
issues.detail: serialize/deserialize treat resample() output as None-or-sized-bytes-like, then later passed to WebSocket send or InputAudioRawFrame. The invariant 'resample returns bytes or None' is not stated locally and not enforced by a type annotation visible here. A one-line comment naming the contract (and a cast if needed) would let a reader verify correctness without chasing create_stream_resampler.

review.summary: The Vonage serializer is straightforward and largely correct, but the FastAPI transport's packetization patch is UNDER-AUDITED: the loop invariant for _audio_send_buffer is unstated, termination of partial tail bytes is not handled, and the advertised 'real-time pacing' is not actually implemented. The buffer is also a WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE choice — bytearray slice-deletion is O(n) where a deque or memoryview would be O(1). The serializer would benefit from NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT treatment around the resampler contract and DTMF schema ambiguity. None of these are correctness emergencies, but the patch reads as code-as-compiler-input rather than code-as-explanation. State the invariants, fix the tail-flush, and either implement pacing or retract the claim.
